title: A2 Grammar Quiz 1 — Past Simple, Comparatives, Going To

questions.question: She ___ TV last night.
questions.explanation: Regular Past Simple → add -ed: 'watched'.

questions.question: They ___ to music yesterday.
questions.explanation: Regular verb 'listen' → Past Simple: 'listened'.

questions.question: I ___ to the market this morning.
questions.explanation: 'Go' is irregular. Past Simple → 'went'. 'Gone' is the past participle (used with have/has).

questions.question: She ___ a great book last week.
questions.explanation: 'Read' is irregular — the Past Simple spelling is the same ('read') but the pronunciation changes: /rɛd/.

questions.question: He ___ his keys yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Lose' is irregular. Past Simple → 'lost'.

questions.question: We ___ to the party. We stayed home.
questions.explanation: Negative Past Simple → 'didn't + base verb'. Never 'didn't went'.

questions.question: ___ you see that film?
questions.explanation: Question in Past Simple → 'Did + subject + base verb?'

questions.question: The weather ___ terrible yesterday.
questions.explanation: Past of 'is' → 'was'. Used with singular subjects.

questions.question: ___ your parents at home last night?
questions.explanation: 'Parents' is plural → 'Were'. Question: 'Were + subject + ...?'

questions.question: She ___ dancing. (stop)
questions.explanation: Short vowel + single consonant → double the consonant: 'stopped'.

questions.question: This box is ___ than that one.
questions.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y → change y to i, add -er: 'heavier'.

questions.question: English is ___ than maths for me.
questions.explanation: Short adjective ending in -y → 'easier'. Never 'more easier' (double comparative).

questions.question: This film is ___ than the book.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives (3+ syllables) → use 'more + adjective': 'more interesting'.

questions.question: She sings ___ than her sister.
questions.explanation: 'Good' has an irregular comparative: 'better'. 'Best' is the superlative.

questions.question: That is the ___ building in the city.
questions.explanation: Superlative of short adjectives → 'the + adjective + -est': 'the tallest'.

questions.question: It's the ___ day of my life.
questions.explanation: Irregular superlative: good → better → 'the best'.

questions.question: I ___ visit my grandmother tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' = am/is/are + going to + base verb. Used for plans and intentions.

questions.question: She ___ study medicine.
questions.explanation: 'She' → 'is going to + base verb'.

questions.question: We ___ stay late.
questions.explanation: Negative: 'aren't going to + base verb'.

questions.question: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used for predictions based on opinion/thought: 'I think it will...'.

questions.question: I ___ help you. Just ask me.
questions.explanation: 'Will' ('ll) is used for spontaneous offers or decisions made at the moment of speaking.

questions.question: ___ people were at the party?
questions.explanation: 'How many' is used with countable nouns: 'people' is countable.

questions.question: ___ water do you drink a day?
questions.explanation: 'How much' is used with uncountable nouns: 'water' is uncountable.

questions.question: Is there ___ milk in the fridge?
questions.explanation: 'Any' is used in questions and negative sentences with uncountable/plural nouns.

questions.question: I want ___ water, please.
questions.explanation: 'Some' is used in positive sentences and polite requests: 'I want some water'.

questions.question: She ___ late for work. (0%)
questions.explanation: 'Never' = 0% frequency. It replaces 'don't ever': 'She never comes late'.

questions.question: He ___ watches the news. (100%)
questions.explanation: 'Always' = 100%. It goes before the main verb: 'He always watches'.

questions.question: I ___ him last Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Last Monday' signals a finished past time → Past Simple: 'saw'.

questions.question: She was born ___ a small village.
questions.explanation: 'In' is used with villages, cities, countries: 'born in a village'.

questions.question: My bag is ___ than yours.
questions.explanation: Short adjective 'big' → double g, add -er: 'bigger'. 'More bigger' is wrong (double comparative).
